pizza noun

Traupman 360

pitta, pittae f.

noun, first declension

Libellus VI describes it as a disc of thin bread with cheese and vegetables.

Other words

  • placenta Neāpolītāna — pizza

    also used · modern · Andresian p. 9

    “A Neapolitan flat cake”: classical placenta and Neāpolītānus (Varr., Plin.), a modern phrase.

Examples

  • pittam prandērunt, orbem ē pāne tenuī, cāseō, holeribus

    they had pizza for lunch, a disc of thin bread, cheese and vegetablesLibellus VI, Reditus: per Alpēs domum

See also muffin.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 360.
